messages.subject: chrX and chrY is missing
messages.body_plain:
The pileup files generated by samtool surely contain positions in chrX and chrY, but after I ran pileup2seqz, the output seqz file has no data in chrX and chrY anymore. The other chromosome data seem to be OK.
FYI, the names of the two chromosomes appeared exactly as "chrX", "chrY" in the pileup file.
Thank you ahead for any insights into this.

messages.subject: Re: chrX and chrY is missing
messages.body_plain:
Dear Li,
The seqz should contains all the positions in common of both the two pileup and the gc content files.
A limitation of the process is that the chromosomes need to be in the exact order and with the exact name in all the above mentioned files.

In order to debug further your problem you should list the order of the chromosomes in the two pileup and in the gc content file, to check for any discrepancy in the order on naming (in your case the gc files might be the problem as you already check the pileups).

I usually use the bam2seqz method, in which it is possible to query each individual chromosome separately, this avoid the possible sorting issue and allow to exclude unwanted chromosomes (eg mitochondrial and various alternative patches).

Best

Francesco

messages.subject: Re: chrX and chrY is missing
messages.body_plain:
For exome I generally use all the captured regions. If you have the bed files describing the target regions you can try it. You can try, but probably it will not be enough to solve all the bias issues.

I've observed many times a capture-related bias. This is the results of different efficiency of the targets enrichment protocol (my wild guess actually) in the normal and in the tumor sequencing. Generally this happen when the two experiments are carried in different batches, different time or different labs....

As workaround, we introduced a new parameter in the sequenza-utils.py (--normal2 -n2) that allows to use an alternative not matching (so not from the same patient) normal-sample as "nominator" for the depth ratio.
This is especially helpful if you have a normal sample in every sequencing batch: If you observe a bias, you can use the matching normal sample bam/pileup for the genotype information (with the --normal argument) and the matching-target-efficiency bam/pileup to mitigate the bias in the depth ratio (with the --normal2 argument).

If you use varScan to generate the input, you just need to change the normal pileup used in the "varscan copynumber" program.

Sorry for the contorted explication. If you have any doubt or need further help please keep writing :).

Francesco
